utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I would like to ask you: Do you recognise the woman in this picture? I understand that her back is to us.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alic, I'm going to ask you now: Do you recognise any of the people in this video.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please replay the last bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't identify anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Alic, you testified that when you went -- pardon me. Did you want to say something, sir?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You testified that when you went to the woods to see Mr. Tihic the first time, that he was not wearing a uniform. Yes --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yesterday in the video that the Defence showed you, Mr. Tihic was wearing a uniform. I would like to now show you a still shot of taken from the video that the Defence showed you with Mr. Tihic in a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is from the same Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, you recognise --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you recognise any insignia on the uniform, any marking on the uniform?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do now. The date is right there, so it's not very clear. The date is precisely in the same spot as the armband or marking, if you can remove that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. There's a blue spot there with a white stripe across it, a white stripe crossing the blue shape that looks like a triangle. But I didn't see this when we talked to him. I did not see Ahmo Tihic in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Alic, I understand that. My question is: Now that you do see him in uniform on the video that was shown to you yesterday, do you recognise this insignia, this marking? Does this marking have any -- do you know what this marking is?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This marking is something I saw in Tuzla when I came there in 1995, the lilies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And do you know who or where you would see that marking in Tuzla? Could you just ...

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995, this sort of sign was worn by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you permit, I'm not intending to show or have the next item placed into evidence. It's just that I have a larger photo of that and I would just like Mr. Alic to look at it. We don't expect to tender it. I just want to make sure that there's no confusion in his mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any problem with you, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Only if we can see a copy, obviously. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly. Can I ask the usher first to show this to the Defence and then to Mr. Alic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that we can proceed along these lines in other words, Mr. Jones? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm grateful to the Defence. Can you place it on the ELMO so Your Honours can see it and I'll just ask Mr. Alic one question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, when you look at the image now on your screen before you, is this the image that you saw in Tuzla in 1995?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I saw in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right. And that was an image in connection with the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That's your testimony, correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The BH army in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right. And this is the image that you now recognise in the still shot showing Mr. Tihic? I just want to be clear.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on this image, it's very difficult for me to say whether it's that similar. I can only see a blue shape with a white stripe across it. It's difficult to say. But you must understand that people who came from Tuzla to Srebrenica would bring these uniforms along. And certainly it was possible for one of these to reach Ahmo Tihic. A friend gave it to him or something like that. I don't think that requires too much clarification. But you're asking me what I can see on his arm. I can see a blue shape with a white stripe. It's that simple. Whether the lilies are there or the swords, the crossed swords, is not something that I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, I would ask that this image be removed from the ELMO. And I would like to show Mr. Alic now the next video. Again, we are in the woods with Ahmo Tihic. It's just another segment of P433.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, my question to you right now is: You testified that you went to see Mr. Tihic in the woods on two occasions and one of those occasions was the beginning of August. When you went to see Mr. Tihic, did you see as many men in uniform in the woods with him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I just think this is going to be misleading unless we have clarification as to whether the witness -- where this part of the video is concerned because there isn't a complete continuity on whether this is actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you are right. I think the way to go about it, Ms. Sellers, is to ask the witness whether he noticed any men in uniform because it also depends on whether he was paying particular attention to that in the first place and how many he may have noticed and then you can go on your next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You mean when he went on his visits?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no. First, the witness, we must have confirmation of what he was paying attention to while this video was being shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because he may have been paying attention to other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Jones wanted to have the video placed in a different context. Now, we could go back to where Mr. Jones left off displaying the video yesterday - would add a couple more minutes on - to show how this becomes part of it. So I --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- if I understood Mr. Jones's objection..

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. We could simply ask for this frame, is this still Biljeg, as far as the witness knows. That's where I see it's going to be misleading unless we have this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's another -- that's another good point as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just, then, go back to where the picture of the tent is and then from there we'll proceed again. And I think that will join the two videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you stop as you go along because I was paying attention to uniforms and I was paying attention to other things as well, but I don't know whether the witness was doing the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you recognise the tent that you're seeing in this picture before you as having been the video that the Defence showed you yesterday?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one shown by the Defence yesterday, they showed a tent and I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, do you recognise this scene before you as being in the woods in Biljeg where you met Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say yesterday that I met him here, in this place. I said further up in the woods from here. I didn't see a tent at the time. I saw it yesterday on the video, and I told you that we were all seated at a makeshift table using makeshift chairs made of wood. And I'm not sure why I'm being shown this image again. I know exactly what I said yesterday. Asim, myself, and another two or three persons from Jagodnja and Joseva were there and Ahmo Tihic with the people I mentioned. I didn't see the tent at the time; I saw it yesterday while I was being shown the footage. I've explained as well that at Biljeg where we met, there were no solid buildings, houses, sheds, or anything like that. Nothing of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alic, for that clarification. I would still like to run the video and just ask you a couple questions, even though we understand that you saw Mr. Tihic in the woods at an earlier date. Can you please just look at the images with us again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you see the men in the video in uniform?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see one man wearing a uniform in this image. All the other people appear to be wearing civilian clothes, just plain shirts. So this one person I think is wearing a uniform but not the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Can we continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you see other persons now in the video wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just like the one before, two uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you note an insignia on the uniform as being similar to the insignia that you testified was on the uniform of Mr. Tihic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to see clearly. You can see the white colour and the surrounding blue and the white stripe.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll continue it now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, now are you able to see other men in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see two or three men in uniform there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: All right. We'll continue and be finished with this video in a couple of seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you see what appears to be weapons on the table, on the end of the table?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you were in the JNA and that you developed some skills in weaponry. Could you tell the Trial Chamber, if you know, what types of weapons these are.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Machine-gun, that's what they call it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right. Now, just my last question concerning this video is that you testified earlier, yesterday, that you came to see Ahmo Tihic in the woods in the beginning of August on one of the occasions. This video is in August, and I believe another scene shows it's around the 14th of August. Did Ahmo Tihic have those uniforms and those arms when you came to see him? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Ahmo Tihic didn't have these when we spoke to him. And what you're showing me now, I have no idea where this is. Is this Biljeg? Is this a different village? I explained clearly that Biljeg has no solid buildings, buildings made of solid stuff. And here in this footage we can see some solid buildings in fact, so that leads me to conclude I have no idea where this is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It was that that, as I said earlier, I -- there was bound to be confusion without simply asking him if he knew where this second part, and we saw the difference in time, where that was shot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the witness is completely in control of the situation. He knows exactly where he is. So let's continue, Ms. Sellers, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Would you give me one minute, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to move on but I might have to come back to this. I just want to make sure that the witness will understand the nature of my question in relationship to this video, but I would let my case manager check a couple points for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, within the group that you participated in in Jagodnja, did you ever have members of your armed group, your 10 or 15 men, carry messages to other groups or other places in the area of Jagodnja? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the area of Jagodnja? Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Alic. In the area of Jagodnja.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We from Jagodnja didn't send any messages to anyone, nor did we receive messages from anyone. Only people in search of food would arrive in Jagodnja and Joseva, and from them we would learn what was happening in the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, you testified that at least on two occasions people came to Jagodnja in October 1992 and in January 1993 to ask for your help or to offer you help. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That happened in January when a man arrived from Glogova asking for our help.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And on the 4th or the 5th of October, didn't another group arrive in our area to help you out, to help the group from Jagodnja out?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A group arrived to help us defend ourselves from Kragljivoda. That was the assistance we received.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, how many people were in that group who arrived to help you out?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I explained yesterday, I was a nurse and I was in the village of Hasanovici with the wounded, where in the morning of the 5th of October a man arrived to fetch me. He said I was to go in the direction of Prisalaca Bradva where I found a large number of civilians, and among them there were some armed groups of men. I was able to see 20 to 30 men in one of the groups. I didn't see any other groups. I don't know whether there were others or not; I couldn't see everybody because this was all taking place in a wood. And in a wood you can only see about 200 metres ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I see Madam Vidovic is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, a correction in the transcript. When the witness said -- mentioned Kragljivoda, he said it was the first assistance they had received, whereas in the record it says that was the help we received. I think it's important that the witness said "this was the first help we received."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's an important distinction. Could you please put the question. We want to know exactly what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When the men arrived from Kragljivoda, was that the first time you had ever received assistance from outside?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that's what you said earlier on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Vidovic. Thank you. Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, the person who came to assist you came to specifically request that you, Mr. Alic, participate as a nurse?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically. He only asked me if I was able, and if I wanted to, to go in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did he ask Asim Smajlovic, would he also participate?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did Asim Smajlovic and other members of your group, were they also asked to participate in activities with this person from Kragljivoda?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. The man from Kragljivoda didn't arrive looking for me. You must have misunderstood that. A man arrived from Joseva and he told me what I just said, that is, he asked me if I wanted to go in that direction in order to help the wounded. There wasn't a man coming from Kragljivoda looking for a nurse in Jagodnja to take back with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So where you went to help others was not in Jaglivoda -- I mean, pardon me, was not in Jagodnja and was not in Kragljivoda. You went to another location. The man asked you to go to a third location to help. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're trying to say. I spoke of attacks on Joseva. There were attacks on the village of Joseva on the 3rd, 4th, and 5th on a daily basis. They set fire to our wheat and everything I explained. This group from Kragljivoda arrived to help. And men from my group were in the area of Joseva. I explained that on the map. And where this place, Priselaca is, that's where there was a clash and where fighting continued.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. And, Mr. Alic, on the 5th of October, weren't you assisting the wounded outside of Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was assisting the wounded on the 5th of October at Zanjevski creek, yes. But that happened in the morning of the 5th of October at Priselaca, what I'm talking about. And I was assisting on the 5th of October in Zanjevski Potok. I think I described that well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, you did. You described that very well. And because of that we can have slightly shorter answers because your testimony was clear. I'm just trying to make a couple other points of clarification. Now, did the rest of Asim Smajlovic's group also go towards Fakovici on the 5th of October, as you did?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about 10 to 15 men, including me and two other unarmed men, we were going in the direction of Radijevici. And where the other group was going I really don't know. That evening I returned to Jagodnja at about 2.00 a.m. I think this other group of armed men -- I don't know, actually, whether they stayed in Jagodnja or went looking for food.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did this other group of armed men have a name? Did they refer to themselves as a named group?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What group are you referring to? You mean the one that came to assist us or do you mean the one from our village?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The one that came to assist you, sir.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the group from Kragljivoda.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did they call themselves a group from Kragljivoda or did they call themselves by another name?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard the man who came to get me from Joseva say that a group of men had arrived from Kragljivoda.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you know whether they had a leader, like you had a leader?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that point in time, I didn't know anything. I heard later on that it was Sefik Mandic who was the leader of that group.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when you got to your location near Fakovici, did you see other groups, groups other than your own group, from Jagodnja and Sefik Mandic's group from Kragljivoda? Did you see other groups of armed men?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I crossed that minefield I talked about and entered the village of Abdulici, there was shooting, there were men there who had weapons in the village of Abdulici itself. From the direction of Radijevici and Radijevic Potok there was firing aimed at us. I learned that one of the men there was from Zanjevo. When two men were killed, I went in the direction I described. I arrived at Zanjevski Potok. I didn't go any further. It's all in my statement. I only noticed a large number of civilians --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop. All right. Okay. All right. He's dealt with it -- with the question at the end. Because still then he had not answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was going to ask him the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you see any other armed groups, other than your group? Sefik Mandic's group? Did you see other armed groups?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't see any large groups of armed men, any other large groups of armed men. I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you see any other small groups of Muslim fighters?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I saw a few men in Zanjevo, in Abdulici. And then I went to Zanjevski Potok where I could see only groups of civilians, large numbers of civilians, collecting wheat from the houses in Zanjevo and so on. I didn't enter Fakovici. I said that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, I believe your testimony was that you were in Radijevici, Radijevici Potok, and that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is here that I don't want him to get confused. Radijevici Potok, I suppose. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Radijevici Potok

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And Zanjevski Potok.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's another. There are two Potoks that he mentioned in his testimony in chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, here, no, definitely he mentioned two -- two Potoks. So you need to be very clear whether it's the one or the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, were you in Radijevici Potok when you were taking care of the wounded people from Fakovici, during the Fakovici attack?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please remind us again your location, where you were, when you were taking care of these people, when you were outside of Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Zanjevski Potok.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Zanjevski Potok is below the road from Fakovici on the way to Abdulici. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be shown on the map. I can show you precisely where Zanjevski Potok is on the map. It has -- it's a creek which has its course and there is a bridge crossing it. The creek comes out of the wood and the whole length of the creek is called Zanjevski Potok. And if it's not clear to you, I can show it to you on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He marked it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I think he had, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Or the day before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question is more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Where you were located, could you see every house in Fakovici? Where you were located in Zanjevski Potok, could you see every house in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not every house, but I could see 90 per cent of Fakovici. There is a small bend in Fakovici, and I couldn't see that area. But there are very few houses there. I could see the church, the cafes, the school, the old area, the new area, and so on. I could see 90 per cent of Fakovici from where I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to have the witness shown D135, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I believe that this was shown to you by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would like to draw Mr. Alic's attention to the paragraph that begins with -- and it's one, two, three, fourth paragraph down, "when the shooting stopped I crept behind the arms depot."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, further down in that paragraph it says: "However, when I got to about 10 metres from the detonator, about 100 of them sprang out of hiding, where they were guarding the warehouse. They grabbed me, beat me, and dragged me to my house, which was on fire." Mr. Alic, do you see where I am in the document?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I don't know where that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We'll go down four paragraphs. The paragraph that begins "when the shooting stopped, I crept behind the arms depot."

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. Fine. Now, it says -- within that paragraph it says: "However, when I got to about 10 metres from the detonator, about 100 of them sprang out of hiding where they were guarding the warehouse. They grabbed me, beat me, and dragged me to my house, which was on fire. They knew who I was and they said, 'Now watch us, manager, burn your house.'"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we need to turn the page now.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. In the English version. I don't know whether the page is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. Now page 2. In his case it's page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, my question is -- to you is that: Where you were positioned outside of Fakovici, your testimony was that you didn't see any houses burning. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any houses burning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alic, you've just testified, if I understand correctly, that you didn't see hundreds of Muslim fighters in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, I wasn't in Fakovici. I was at Zanjevski Potok. Zanjevski Potok, as I said, is about a kilometre and a half or two kilometres away from Fakovici. Had there been something burning, I would have seen smoke. You understand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecutor is misinterpreting the text. Soldiers are not mentioned anywhere. It says "I saw a hundred of them." It doesn't say whether they were civilians or soldiers. So you cannot suggest to the witness that they were soldiers. At least that's how it is in the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I stand corrected. I can continue to read the text where it's clarified in the statement. I wanted to take a small part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead, but Ms. Vidovic is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: But, Mr. Alic, your testimony is that you didn't see hundreds of Muslim fighters or tens of Muslim fighters in Fakovici because you were not in Fakovici. That's what I understand. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Alic, were you aware that prisoners, Serb prisoners, were taken by Muslim forces in Fakovici? Just yes or no. Were you aware that that occurred on that day in Fakovici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know anyone by the name of Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I've heard of Zulfo Tursunovic from the refugees who came to collect food in Jagodnja, that he was from Suceska, and that he had a group of men there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Have you heard of Akif Ustic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about him, too. It was the same as with Zulfo. People who came to get food from us who went into the fields, they gave us this information.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And when you say it was the same as with Zulfo, does that mean that you heard that he had a group of armed men -- I'm sorry, that he had a group of men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, the question refers to Akif Ustic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I heard that Akif Ustic had a group of men. I can't recall whether I was told whether these men were armed or not. A lot of time has elapsed and it's hard to remember every detail. It's been 12 or 13 years since then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Have you also heard of Hakija Meholjic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about Hakija Meholjic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you hear that there were also -- he also had a group of armed men?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had some kind of group of armed men. I don't know where he was stationed, but that's what people said. It was rumoured, but whether they were armed and how many of them, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. And then I would like to ask you: Did you hear of Naser Oric during this time period of 1992, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about Naser Oric. These same people said that he was in Potocari and that he has his own group of armed men.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to continue reading this document and then we'll be finished with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I'm going to continue reading the same translation. It said: "They grabbed me, beat me, and dragged me to my house which was on fire. They knew who I was and they said: 'Now, watch us, manager, burn your house down'" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, just to assist you, we are in the same paragraph we were reading earlier on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Alic, I'm just going to move down two or three sentences where it says: "They thought I might be ready to kill myself and take them with me. Behind me went the Turk, or call him what you will, an Ustashi, Zulfo by name. I don't know where he came from. He was tall, older man, dark, with a moustache, and a rather long nose. I heard them call him by his surname, Tursunovic." Is that a description of Zulfo Tursunovic that you would be familiar with?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at no point in time did the witness say that he knew him. He said he'd heard of him, therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree. Therefore that's why my Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. question is would he be familiar with that question. I don't know whether he's seen Mr. Tursunovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then ask him that and then the second question would be legitimate.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that that's what I've asked him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question as I read is as follows: Is that a description of Zulfo Tursunovic that you would be familiar with?" Yeah, but to be familiar with it he must have seen him -- seen him before.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe his testimony has been that he has heard people talk about Zulfo. I don't believe he's testified that he himself right now has seen Zulfo. So people might have described Zulfo to him. And that's why I'm asking this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, are you familiar with this description of Zulfo Tursunovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one ever described him to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Fine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you never saw him in person either? You never saw him in person either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, later on in 1994 I did see him in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So now the question becomes appropriate. I mean, recalling your impression of him, and when you saw him, in 1994, would this be -- rather, you put the question, Ms. Sellers. I mean, once you saw him in 1994, then perhaps you can answer Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you saw him in 1994 with the description given here, agree with the -- of your view of Zulfo Tursunovic? And I will just repeat: "He was a tall, older man, dark, with a moustache and rather long nose." Is that what Zulfo Tursunovic looked like to you in 1994?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. No, no, no. Zulfo Tursunovic looked perfectly normal. He had a perfectly normal nose. I don't know about this bit about the long nose or rather long nose. I'm not sure what that's supposed to mean exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Well, how old was Zulfo Tursunovic when you saw him in 1994?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Two years older --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is something that I can't say. Can't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did he have at that time a moustache? Was he tall? Was he, let's say, over 50 years old?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly how old he was, but in my estimate he may have been about 50, 55 perhaps. That's what I reckoned. He did wear a moustache. That's all I know. When I first looked at him -- well, you know, people change. The way people look changes over time. People were starving, but that bit about the big nose, that part is certainly not true. He did not have a long nose.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Mr. Alic. And, Mr. Alic, I would like to ask you, did you know who was the manager of the post office in Fakovici in 1992 or referred to --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. A person referred to as the manager from the post office?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I might even know the person, but I don't know the person's first or last name. I don't know the person's name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you describe the person, if you remember, to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I just can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. Would you just give me one second to check with my case manager on the other issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask at this time if we could go back to the video for a very small period. But --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I'm going to show you the video that the Defence showed you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you recognise in this video the place where you went to in the woods with Mr. Smajlovic to see Ahmo Tihic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not the same place that we were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. So this was a different place then where you had visited him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it's a very generic image of a forest. It's very difficult to say which forest this might be.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just wanted to clarify that it was neither section of the tape for which he visited. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, right now I would like to move toward January of 1993, and yesterday you testified about your participation in an attack in Jedjeska -- Jezestica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't agree that he characterised it as an attack. He went to help in Glogova. It's a small point, but still we should get it right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Thank you, Mr. Jones. Yes, Ms. Sellers. You would avoid the word -- using the word "attack."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, yesterday you testified that Ejub Golic or his representative came to your group in Jagodnja. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's correct that he sent someone over to Jagodnja.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the person that he sent over?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was the person armed, carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did he speak to you or did he speak to Asim Smajlovic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To Asim Smajlovic, that's who he talked to. There were people there in the village and he was there, too, so he sought assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, did Asim Smajlovic then ask the members of the group that you were in whether they wanted to go, follow this man, to assist Glogova?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alic, I believe that you agreed to go?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, was a decision taken to leave immediately, or were you allowed to say, I would leave in a week or two weeks?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It wasn't taken immediately. It was on the 3rd or the 4th I believe. It was around the 5th, I can't remember specifically, that we left for Glogova whether it was the 4th or the 5th, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you know whether you had to be in Glogova at any specific time?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no way we could predict the time that we would get there. We had been told we should count on about two days travel time on foot to Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you know whether Glogova was expecting you to arrive at any specific time?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't think they knew that we were coming.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Why do you say that, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man who came to ask for our help, those people of Glogova, there was no way for them to know whether we would ever leave or whether we would ever arrive. So he was travelling to us, and there was no way they could have known that we had left. We could as well -- just as well not have left to begin with, so they didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was this man carrying any form of hand-held radio or any form of communication?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did anyone in your group have any form of communication, such as a hand-held radio, or a ham-operated radio?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Alic -- excuse me. So it's your testimony this man came, he proposed that Asim Smajlovic's group follow him to Glogova, and you decided to leave when you wanted to, you decided to take as much time as you wanted to to get to Glogova. Would that be your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man came and asked for help -- requested our help. He asked for help. Was that -- he asked for help. He asked us to go. And as soon as we believed we were ready to go, we set out to help those people who had been jeopardised by the Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, as you were travelling via Bajramovici to Cizmici, did any of your group decide that I want to go back home or I want to go to another location, or did everyone stay together?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The group that set out stuck together all the way to Cizmici. We moved together.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you meet any other groups in the forest going in that direction toward Glogova?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't -- I didn't see anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So your testimony would be that it was just this armed group of 10 or 15 men that were going through the woods, guided by this man, toward Glogova to help out Ejub Golic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, were you carrying a weapon at that time?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And if I'm correct, you have not -- or you did not carry a weapon throughout the summer of 1992 up until January of 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I was not carrying a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ever carry a weapon? Let me rephrase that because how it's said in English could be misleading. Did you ever carry a weapon as a member of Asim Smajlovic's group?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: After the shooting, the heavy firing, in Fakovici, did you ever ask to carry a weapon or think you should carry a weapon?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one asked me to. I was so busy as I was that there was no need for me to have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Whenever weapons would be captured, such as your testimony with the truck that had the red cross on it, were members of Asim Smajlovic's group given new weapons or other weapons?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'd like to know whether when weapons were captured by Mr. Smajlovic's group such as the time period or on the occasion when the red -- the truck with the red cross was captured, were members of the group ever given those weapons?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was no truck; it was a car. That's the first thing --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... vehicle.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those weapons stayed with us in Smajlovic's group in the village of Jagodnja and Joseva only.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So do I take it that the other men from the group who had weapons would protect you because you were one member of the group who never had a weapon?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course we had to protect one another.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And so, the members of the group knew that you didn't have a weapon, and weren't you especially protected?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course they knew. They saw it for themselves, didn't they? Of course one knew how someone who was carrying no weapon was supposed to be moving about. You can't be the first to go. You know where the nurse is supposed to be, a nurse carrying bandages and medicines. I think that is self explanatory.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I agree, because the nurse is particularly vulnerable and important for the group.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, in the other groups that you met, whether it's in Fakovici - and we'll talk about Jezestica - were there other people who were nurses or performed the function of nurse in the groups?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, it was in the other group that came from Kragljivoda, those who came across the minefield where four people were killed. A nurse was one of the persons killed from one of the villages that I can't remember now. A nurse tripped over one of the mines, stepped on it, and was killed. In Zanjevo I didn't notice anyone marked out as a nurse or carrying first-aid kits, that is with the exception of myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I just have a couple of questions to ask you about Cizmici. When you arrived in Cizmici, did you notice any other armed grouped -- armed groups of men in Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time when I arrived with the group, it was dark. We entered a house, as I said. We rested and ate whatever food we had brought along. We spent the night there. I didn't see anyone else. The next morning, we left at daybreak. We left Cizmici at daybreak or earlier. It must have been 2.00 or 3.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And you left at 2.00 or 3.00 a.m., and at that point you didn't see any other armed groups leaving in the direction in which you were going?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We saw a group of civilians moving, a large one, a group that was in the area. We walked across creeks and mountainous areas that were snowed over. It was very difficult to walk. You just tried to see -- you just tried to decide which path you would take and you were mindful of not stepping on anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that the only armed group was in fact your group with the guide that Ejub Golic had sent to you? Are those the only armed group?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm sure Ms. Sellers is not trying to get the witness to say in the whole of the area this witness is claiming to say that there was only one armed group. He's obviously talking about Cizmici --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- the particular route he took, what was in his vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That's fine, but his answer shouldn't be purported to be about a broader area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sellers, I think you should make it clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When he left the house in the morning and I want to know if there was any other armed group walking with him from Cizmici that morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Like I said, we left the next morning. It was still dark. We noticed a large number of civilians moving along, but I did not see any armed groups. You understand that it was dark and you couldn't see a thing right there in the middle of the forest. I said this once and now you're asking me the same question again. So to sum it up, I did not see any major groups of armed people in Cizmici that night, with the exception of the people who were carrying rucksacks, but those people were civilians, to put it simply.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right. So I have this one last question before we take the break, Your Honour. Mr. Alic, you testified that you were given ribbons to wear around your head. Why was your armed group given ribbons to wear around their head in Cizmici?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why or how. I got one myself, tied it around my head. I never asked any questions as to why I was supposed to wear it, but it was probably in order to mark us out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I can stop here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I'll remind you that we were talking about your group in Cizmici and your testimony was that you in fact ended up in Jezestica on that morning of January 7th, 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, when you came out of the woods and into Jezestica, did you see any other group of armed fighters other than Asim Smajlovic's group?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When we came near Jezestica, there was heavy firing, a lot of shooting, and there were lots of civilians there who were walking ahead of us, quite literally. On the other hand, I did notice people with rifles but I had no idea which group they belonged to or where they'd come from. I really didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. And can I just ask, yes or no, were the other people that you noticed with rifles, did you know them to be Muslims or did you assume Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that they were Muslims and not Serbs?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the forest where we were, the people who were around me, at least that's what I believed, were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alic, it's true that you never made it to Glogova. Your group walked for two days, stopped overnight, but you never went to Glogova, did you?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in Cizmici, and that night we were told that we would go in the direction of Glogova. Now, where did we end up? I don't know. We weren't familiar with the area. I'm not sure how we ended up where we did. But it was from my return from Jezestica that I reached Avdagine Njive with some wounded and walked from there towards Jezestica. That's what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: After you participated in this armed fighting, you returned to Jagodnja. You didn't go to Glogova, did you.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I passed through Glogova with the wounded, and I withdrew towards Cizmici on the same day from Avdagine Njive, which is part of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, during that whole day, did you see armed groups wearing uniforms -- Muslim armed groups, whether they were white uniforms, whether they were camouflage uniforms, whether they were old JNA uniforms. Did you see any uniformed people?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those firing from the Serb houses, those were Serb soldiers wearing uniforms. As for the Muslims who had arrived from the same direction as myself, there were no people wearing uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, I'm not speaking now specifically about people arriving from your direction. I'm asking about people you've seen during that entire day, and I'm not asking about Serbs, I'm asking any Muslim fighters or forces. Did you see anyone in any form of uniform, any type of uniform? Just yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And any of the wounded that you cared for, were any of those wounded wearing uniforms or have ribbons tied around their heads?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. None of them were in uniform. Those wounded were civilians, and I dressed their wounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you meet any of the fighters from Glogova, other than the man who guided you?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So then it's your testimony that you walked for two days and participated in what appears to be large-scale armed fighting and never met the fighters or the soldiers from Glogova. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met none of the armed soldiers from Glogova. I was involved in the Jezestica area. We came down to Jezestica and I entered two or three houses. I must repeat what I said yesterday because that's what you're asking me about. I entered two or three houses and the bakery before I entered any other houses. There were wounded civilians there, and for that reason I left for Avdagine Njive and Cizmici, where I waited for my group in order to go back to Jagodnja. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. And you can't assist us with any of the military formations, if any, that were there. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can't tell you anything about any military formations at this time or any other major groups. I saw none of those. I did my own job and I know exactly what it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Mr. Alic. I'm now going to turn to three other brief areas and then I'll be concluding my direct examination. Mr. Alic, you testified to the Trial Chamber earlier today about the names of certain people that you said came from -- one from Jagodnja, that was Ahmed Alic, and others that you were familiar with in Joseva.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, Madam Prosecutor, you'll have to repeat the first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Let me repeat it. Ahmed Alic.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahmed Alic, no such man at Jagodnja. It can only be Ahmet.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Ahmet, right.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No person called Ahmed because that's a different name altogether.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It does end in a "t." Do you remember when you testified at the very beginning of your testimony today about these names, including Hasib Kurtic, Fahrudin Avdic, Ferid Bektic. You recall that testimony, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like the witness to be shown Prosecution Exhibit 571, please. And I would like to also hand up to the Trial Chamber and to Defence a translation of some of the items within P71. I'm sorry, it's P571.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I'm going to speak a bit more rapidly. If you cannot understand what I'm saying, please indicate. But I just would like to be able to conclude the cross-examination in the coming minutes. You've been given a list of the members of the Biljeg TO unit, Srebrenica. And you will see on the page that ends in ERN 703, I believe it's 02115703, that it states the name, place of birth, and residence, when the person joined the TO, the duty of that person, whether they were a member of the unit. If you look under number 1 you see the name Ahmo Tihic, born in 1955. It states that he joined the Biljeg TO in April of 1992 and that he was a unit commander. Is that consistent also with what you've testified about to the Trial Chamber, that Ahmed Tihic -- Ahmo Tihic was the commander of the Biljeg group?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahmo Tihic was the commander or the leader of the Biljeg group, but not at the date stated here. I saw Ahmo Tihic at the time I mentioned in my statement, at Biljeg. I didn't hear of his being there before that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. And you're referring to July -- June and July or August of 1992. Correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. End of July or beginning of August. I did not hear of the existence of these formations before that, nor did I see them at Biljeg, what you're showing me now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Would you just also look further down on number 2, and now I'm looking over in the column that says "duty." It's one, two, thee, four, five, I believe the sixth column over. Do you see under where, for Ahmo Tihic it said unit commander, that we have deputy commander, we have the word "courier," and further down on line number 4 we have "cook." Do you see where the document states those functions in the unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. -- this way you're bound to confuse the witness because you mentioned line 2 and you mentioned line 4. These are not on line 2 and on line 4 but other numbers. Deputy commander seems to be in line 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And cook I could see is -- the Serbian word is under 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Under line 7. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you see those functions listed under those columns?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see what it says here. I can see what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like you now to turn to number 87 on this list --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. It's number 95.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could you turn to number 95 on the list.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you see the name Fahrudin Avdic?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And wasn't it your testimony before you confirmed that Fahrudin Avdic is from Joseva?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is from Joseva.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like you to turn further in the list, and you will see that it on ERN that ends in 710, the ERN is 02115710 at the very bottom of the list, it ends in the number 127.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see 127.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: All right. And if you turn over on the next page that would end in ERN number 711. That would be 02115711. We have what is basically the same, Biljeg TO, Srebrenica, except for it says A4/1. And that list ends in number 9. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alic, you would agree with me that 127 and 9 adds up to 136?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you need the witness to confirm that -- this or --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Can we take judicial notice of that. Our first judicially noticed fact, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And also for the sake of expediency, Mr. Alic, there are the names of other people you've confirmed that come from Joseva in the document. I will not run through them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would now, while this document is here, ask that the witness be shown P80, please. And I would direct the Trial Chamber's attention to page number 2 in P80 under number 4. And I believe that that would be the same for the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alic, do you see under number 4 where it says "TO Biljeg, Biljeg Company, A4, A4/1, 136 conscripts, Commander Ahmo Tihic"?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. We can remove the documents from Mr. Alic. I just have two very brief areas to go into now. Can we have a P number for the translation. I believe that we have P571 for the document, but the translation would be new, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, this list which indicates names under 1, 2, 3, up to 117, 118? In other words, this list that was circulated a few minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and this list corresponds to the names --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's okay. I'm not questioning that. I mean, I'm just trying to make sure that we have the right document. What's the next number, please, Madam Registrar? P5 --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P587, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this document which is supposed to be extracted or contains details from P571 is being tendered and received and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P587, and it consists of one page only.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, yesterday the Defence asked you a series of questions pertaining to whether certain people lived in Joseva or Jagodnja. And if I can remind you of your testimony, they referred you to Prosecution exhibit, asking you, Did you see number 16, Osman Salkic, Joseva. And you said: "I see this number and there isn't a person under that name at Joseva. The family does not exist in Joseva, Osman." And they also asked you about a Hasan Salkic, and you repeated the testimony that these persons did not exist in Joseva. Do you remember that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I'd like to ask you: Are you aware or do you know that there are towns that bear the same name as Joseva or districts within that area of Bosnia and Serbia? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean that area of Bosnia and Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, more specifically, Srebrenica municipality --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And across the Drina --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And across the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And across the Drina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Alic, I take that you would be familiar that there are five towns with the name -- or five areas with the name Joseva?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would now like to pass up a Prosecution exhibit that I was able to show to the Defence prior to the commencement of this session. And this exhibit is part of the census pertaining to one of those other places. I have given to the Defence, and now Your Honours are in possession of it, the letter that we received. I have to ask that we go into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go into private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: A new document consisting of three pages, one of which is two -- four-sided. With ERN 00671997, 00671998, and the rest which contains the names of several persons living in Fojhar Srebrenica, Joseva, is being tendered, and received, and marked as Defence Exhibit P588 -- Prosecution Exhibit, sorry. Prosecution Exhibit P588.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, you testified yesterday that when you were in Srebrenica after the demilitarisation, that UNPROFOR wouldn't allow people to carry weapons. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And your testimony was also that they dealt fairly harshly with people who did carry weapons.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard what I said yesterday. The man who was in the direction of the old town, this group of UNPROFOR soldiers chased him away. He was probably carrying a rifle.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard and that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like Mr. Alic now just to look at a very short video. It's about 30 -- maybe about one minute. Okay. This is P318. A transcript accompanies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see anything on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's start again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the writing on the screen. It suggests the name of one of the people in the picture. That's not acceptable in our submission. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Because if there's any question asked to this witness about any of the people, it's just been suggested to him or fed to him that one of the people is our client. If there's no -- if no question is asked about that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what the question is going to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: But I would object to any question about who's in the picture because it's already cued below the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not going to change much, Mr. Jones, because we can see it, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I believe the objection is premature because any questions I had did not go to the nature of identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So lets continue seeing and then we'll see what the question ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have just understood by my case manager that we're experiencing a little difficulty in having the transcript continue to roll down. And if I understand correctly, we are probably past the point of what we see on the written screen. Could I just have that confirmed by a speaker, B/C/S speaker, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I did of course notice that the script did not scroll any further, but I thought that you had actually stopped it yourself, as you're not interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We were interested in continuing down until the time period where we see the writing. If it's proceeded past that, then we don't want to prolong the tape in any way. So I just wanted to make sure that it has gone down to cover the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, as far as I'm concerned, I could hear nothing of what was said in Bosnian here. And I'm really interested in how someone managed to produce a transcript of it. I don't know if the witness was able to hear anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, were you able to hear anything in a language you understand from the tape?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very poorly, hardly anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If necessary, Ms. Sellers, we'll play it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll play the sound louder. If we do that one last time I won't belabour the Trial Chamber's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course I was hearing sound. But you asked me when I wasn't even trying to see if I could understand what was being said in that language. I mean -- and I thought that you had stopped the script rolling because of reasons of your own. So I was anxiously waiting for the question or questions, actually.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I suggest that Mr. Alic's microphone be turned up here and that does significantly augment the sound. Can I ask the usher to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's ask him first whether he's heard better this time. I think -- my sound level without touching anything here was higher in any case.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, have you been able to hear the Bosnian on this tape better this time, the second time we've played it?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little better, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher just to adjust it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just don't ruin his eardrum, Madam Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop, because we haven't covered the previous part again. It continued from where we had left it when you stood up to ask for an increase in the sound level.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We're going to just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the best thing at this point in time is to leave everything tomorrow because you're not going to finish in three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to finish in three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But is there going to be a re-examination, for sure. It doesn't take much to understand that there is a re-examination and I understand that we have got some questions of our own.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I would have been ten minutes to finish with this witness today --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But I am not going to keep anyone else -- anyone for another ten minutes. We have been sitting long enough, so he will come for a half an hour at most in the morning and then he can be taken to the airport straight away. The arrangements can remain in place and he can be taken to the airport.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, and then I will continue tomorrow morning. I will be two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It doesn't make sense because I do understand going beyond a certain time does create problems. It doesn't create problems to us, but -- especially people who are using their hands and whatever. It does create problems, and I understand that, and I have every duty to respect those concerns. So, yeah, let's leave it at that. You will return back for a very short time tomorrow morning. In the meantime, I take it -- Madam Usher, please, if you could communicate with the Victims and Witnesses Section, they can proceed with the arrangements for his return to his place of residence, but he will be needed here for a short while. If it is problematic for the Victims and Witnesses Unit and we need to start at 8.00 instead of 9.00 -- because I don't know what time the flight would be. I haven't got an idea. So if we need to come at 8.00, would everyone be willing to come here at 8.00? Judge Eser? Judge Brydensholt? And I think that would be possible. I don't figure that that should present any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's fine with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, because I want to make sure that he goes home. I can't -- honestly, I would -- you know that I have stayed for 10 minutes, 15 minutes, sometimes even beyond that. But I have decided that that will not be repeated unless it is absolutely, absolutely necessary. So shall we meet tomorrow again at 8.00? I don't know. I mean, I don't know what time the flight is. Yes, yes she is going to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You will have to come back as well, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: That's not a problem, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know it's not a problem. We would have dealt with your problem tomorrow in any case.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Di Fazio, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What I was going to suggest is -- is that if the Defence could see a way to finishing in a reasonably short amount of time, I could put what I have to say in a couple of A4 pages and have it to you and to the Defence. Tomorrow we wouldn't even have to convene. I have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I have to have the agreement -- Mr. Di Fazio, I have to have the agreement of everyone here. I understand that past an hour and a half it becomes difficult for -- so it's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All I'm saying is, it's no problem for the Prosecution to reduce what I've got to say into writing, and the Defence could look at it at their leisure and have plenty of time and come back on Tuesday next week. I'm more than willing to do that. I don't need stand here and say what I've got to say. I could put it in writing. That would then leave my friend and Mr. Jones --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But do you have it in writing already, or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I haven't. I will type it up and then I send it to you by tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That could be done if it is acceptable to the Defence. I don't know. Is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, it is. We would -- we, really -- for this witness and for everyone we would really prefer to finish with his testimony today and we can be ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will make an effort, Mr. Jones. I would imagine there are no problems on this side. You think it's okay with you. All right. The interpreters, another 15 minutes, maximum?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Technicians? Okay. I'm being told if he stays tomorrow he can't leave tomorrow then he has to leave -- he will be leaving on Saturday. Let's make an effort -- the technicians, I haven't -- all right. Please, could you bring your cross-examination to an end as quickly as possible. And then, Mr. Jones, please try to limit your re-examination to what is really essential so that we will go home. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that now the film is just being rebooted at the proper place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
