utterances.text: Mr. Alic, let me just ask you: Do you confirm your testimony that when UNPROFOR came to Srebrenica, that the carrying of heavy weapons and artillery was not allowed under demilitarisation?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. I didn't see any people in Srebrenica carrying weapons in or around Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I can finish here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Ms. Sellers. Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, just a few questions and if you can keep your answers as short as possible. In the video we've just seen, we've seen some men in uniform. Are you able to tell us where that was filmed?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Are you even able to say whether it's in the Srebrenica area?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I think it was in the general area of Srebrenica because we were in a small enclave where nothing like this could take place. So this was not in the Srebrenica area, to the extent that I was familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. And are you able to tell us when this was shot, whether it was 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995, 1996?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way I could say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And there's reference to one of the persons there talking about Chetniks. Is "Chetniks" an expression to refer to Serb soldiers or does it refer to Serb civilians as well?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The expression is used for Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, going back to the new exhibit P588?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, firstly the Prosecution suggested to you that there were five places with the name Joseva in the Srebrenica area. That's not something you can confirm, is it? You haven't heard of five other places?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't. That's exactly what I said originally.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And on this document do you agree that the settlement referred to is in fact Fojhar? If you look at the document and you see the column at the top, settlement, and then it actually says "Fojhar."

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no translation here. It says "Fojhar" down here, but I have no idea what the English means.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. At the top of that column where it says "Fojhar," the very top, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read English.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: My apologies. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll trust the Chamber will take note of what I've just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What are you referring to exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: In this document we have the columns. The settlement is Fojhar, according to this. We see Joseva, but it doesn't say that it's a settlement, it doesn't say anything about Joseva, simply that that's the first point. Your Honours can take note of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Then if we look at that -- on this document, I asked you yesterday about a Hasan Salkic. Hasan is a man's name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you see the name Hasa Salkic. Do you agree that that's a woman's name?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hasa, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: So there's no Hasan Salkic, in fact, on this list, is there?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes there is not or yes there is?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was not interpreted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I -- you need to repeat the question. And I think it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Again, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it -- you can script this question into the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness please be shown P571 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'm going to take you to some names in this document and I want you to tell me whether they were living in Joseva from May 1992 on onwards or not and the first is Sadija -- Kurtic Hajdar Sadija?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would just ask him to specify which Joseva they were living in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Joseva that they were living in.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I'll take it number by number. In number 7 the question is: For each of these whether they were living in the Joseva which is next to Jagodnja from May 1992 onwards. So on the first page, number 7, Kurtic, Hajdara Sadija.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kurtic Hajdar Sadija, no not from Joseva, number 7. Kurtic Hajdara Sadija, no, no, this person is not from Joseva.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Not from the Joseva next to Jagodnja?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, if you would turn to page 02115708 and it's numbers 87, 88, and 95. Kurtic Mehana Hasib, was he living in your Joseva from May 1992 onwards?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man is from Joseva, but he wasn't living there at the time. His house had been torched, so he went elsewhere. I'm not sure where to.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the same question for 88, Bektic Rame Dzevad, if it is Dzevad.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same answer applies to this person. One thing you need to understand: People left Jagodnja and Joseva, those people whose houses had been torched. I'm not sure where they -- all of them went. When they ran out of food, they would come back for food and leave again, but they left the village. They weren't there, they weren't living there, I've explained this twice already, haven't I.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: To cut it short then, does that refer to all the names we see from Joseva, number 95 on that page Avdic Manuta [phoen] Fahrudin.

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the next page number 100 Bektic Akmer [phoen] Ferid?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And the next ones 117, 118, 119, Alic Osman Ahmet, Kurtic Nedzad Fadil, and Kurtic --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Alic Osmana Ahmet is a relative of mine. He was married to someone from the area. He and his wife left the village all together, left Jagodnja I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, as far as this reference to unit in Biljeg is concerned, when you went to Biljeg and you saw Ahmo and his men, did there appear to you to be soldiers in properly formed units?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Those were no properly formed units like you said. They were more civilians than soldiers. That's at least the -- how they looked in their civilian wear, their regular plain T-shirts, sports shoes. When I say a "soldier," we all know what that implies, uniform, weapons, equipment, and all the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And was there anything like 136 of those men when you were there in Biljeg in the summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I told you who I talked to and how many people were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Now, a few last questions. You were asked about your task as a -- or what you did as a nurse. When you helped people as a nurse, was it always at the request of Asim Smajlovic or did you just do it because that's what you were trained to do?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did this out of sheer love, as it were. I was trying to help those people who had been struck by misfortune.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And you helped civilians as much as fighters, did you not?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indiscriminately, irregardless of whether these people were civilians, soldiers, or even heads of cattle. We had wounded cattle whose lives we tried to save, let alone people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And if you had seen someone who had been injured by artillery or by a mortar and Asim Smajlovic told you to leave them alone, would you do that or would you tend to them?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a humanitarian job, the way I saw it. I would have gone and helped every person facing that sort of situation. Asim was in no position to order me to go there or not to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one matter relating to the interview which you were shown and there was a reference to couriers. Could you just clarify this for us, and, please, with a yes or no: The Almas that you referred to that came from Srebrenica to Biljeg, he went to Biljeg, didn't he, he wasn't sent to Jagodnja and Joseva?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And he wasn't, from what you heard, sent to gather --

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained this, I think. I made it quite clear. Alma Hasanovic was sent to Biljeg and not to Jagodnja and Joseva. So that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Answer by yes or no because you're going to come again tomorrow like this. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, I have two more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And please do answer with yes or no so we can finish. You didn't hear, did you, that he was sent to gather information on how many weapons or how many fighters there are in Biljeg, that he was sent to take over from Ahmo?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never heard that he had been sent there to gather information on how many weapons there were or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now -- and also you -- when you were asked about what you heard of Naser Oric you said that it was the -- that he was the same as Hakija and Zulfo and Akif, in other words that he had a group of men, and that his group was in Potocari. Correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Now, did you hear in interview it being said by the person who was being interviewed: "After I was elected to be commander, in practice I was basically the same as I had been before. There was still the Territorial Defence units and I was still the commander of the Territorial Defence units. In practice, I stayed a soldier, as I had been before." Do you recall hearing that?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: When you say that Naser Oric had his group, as Hakija and Zulfo and Akif did, is it your evidence that essentially he had his group and it was in Potocari and they had their groups, which were elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that Naser Oric had a group at Potocari and that all the other persons that I referred to had their own groups in their own villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: And when Asim and his group went to Cizmici, did Asim at that point have a superior who he reported to or not?

utterances.speaker: IBRO ALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Jones. Mr. Alic, we've managed to conclude with your testimony. I wish to thank you for having come over. You will be receiving the assistance of our staff to facilitate your return back home. On behalf of everyone, I should like to wish you a safe journey back home. You can now leave the courtroom. I also wish to publicly thank everyone here for having accepted to overstay, particularly you, Madam, because I know how difficult it is for you to stay keying in for more than an hour and a half and this has been quite demanding. We'll meet again on Tuesday then. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 25th day of October, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
